name: Nairobi
tagline: The capital with lions on its doorstep
intro: Kenya's capital and biggest city, a busy business hub for East Africa. It is the only capital city in the world with a national park inside its city limits, so you can see giraffes and rhinos with skyscrapers behind them.
climate: Mild all year thanks to the altitude: warm days, cool evenings. Long rains roughly March–May, short rains roughly October–December. June–August can feel chilly.
airport: Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (NBO), ~15–20 km from the CBD; Wilson Airport for domestic and safari flights

neighbourhoods.name: CBD
neighbourhoods.note: The city centre: offices, government buildings, matatu stages and markets. Busy by day, quieter at night.

neighbourhoods.name: Westlands
neighbourhoods.note: Offices, malls, restaurants and the city's best-known nightlife strip.

neighbourhoods.name: Kilimani
neighbourhoods.note: Leafy, central and popular with young professionals; lots of apartments and cafés.

neighbourhoods.name: Karen
neighbourhoods.note: Spacious, green suburb near the Giraffe Centre and Karen Blixen Museum.

neighbourhoods.name: Lavington
neighbourhoods.note: Quiet, residential and upmarket, with good restaurants.

neighbourhoods.name: Gigiri
neighbourhoods.note: Home of the UN offices and many embassies; calm and secure-feeling.

neighbourhoods.name: Eastleigh
neighbourhoods.note: A bustling trading district known for wholesale shopping and Somali food.

moneyTips: M-Pesa is accepted almost everywhere, even at small kiosks.
Cards work in malls, hotels and bigger restaurants; carry some cash for matatus and markets.
ATMs are easy to find; use ones inside banks or malls.
Keep some KSh 50 and 100 notes for small purchases; KSh 1,000 notes can be hard to break.
transport: Matatus (shared minibuses) go everywhere and are cheap but can be confusing at first.
Uber, Bolt and other apps are widely used and easy for visitors.
Boda bodas are fast in traffic; ask for a helmet.
Traffic is heavy at rush hour, so allow extra time.
The SGR train to Mombasa leaves from the Nairobi Terminus near Syokimau.
food: Nyama choma (grilled meat) with kachumbari and ugali.
Chapati and beans or stew at local cafés.
Mandazi and chai for breakfast.
A wide international restaurant scene in Westlands and Kilimani.
safety: Like many big cities, petty theft happens: keep phones out of sight on busy streets.
Use an app or a known taxi at night rather than walking long distances.
Ask your hosts which areas they recommend; most visitors feel comfortable in the main suburbs.

cost.reason: Kenya's priciest city for rent, dining out and hotels.

transport.reason: Apps make it easy, but traffic jams are serious.

climate.reason: Mild all year thanks to the altitude.

safety.reason: Normal big-city caution needed, especially at night.

nightlife.reason: Lively bars, clubs and live music, especially in Westlands.

verify: Scores are editorial estimates. Confirm JKIA distance and SGR terminus location.

name: Mombasa
tagline: Kenya's historic Indian Ocean port
intro: Kenya's second city and main port, on an island linked to the mainland by bridges and the Likoni ferry. Swahili culture, an old town of narrow streets, Fort Jesus and beaches north and south of the city.
climate: Hot and humid all year. Main rains roughly April–June. Cooler, breezier months are around July–September.
airport: Moi International Airport (MBA)

neighbourhoods.name: Old Town
neighbourhoods.note: Narrow lanes, carved doors and Swahili architecture next to Fort Jesus.

neighbourhoods.name: Nyali
neighbourhoods.note: Upmarket mainland suburb north of the island, with beaches, malls and hotels.

neighbourhoods.name: Bamburi
neighbourhoods.note: Beach hotels and a relaxed holiday feel, further north.

neighbourhoods.name: Shanzu
neighbourhoods.note: Quiet beach resorts north of Bamburi.

neighbourhoods.name: Mombasa Island (town centre)
neighbourhoods.note: Markets, offices and the famous Tusks on Moi Avenue.

neighbourhoods.name: Diani (south coast)
neighbourhoods.note: Well-known beach resort south of the city, across the Likoni ferry, in Kwale County.

moneyTips: M-Pesa works everywhere, just as in Nairobi.
Beach hotels often quote in US dollars; local places use shillings.
Agree tuk-tuk fares before you set off.
Bargain politely at curio stalls near Fort Jesus and the beaches.
transport: Tuk-tuks are everywhere and cheap for short trips.
Matatus connect the island with the north and south coast.
The Likoni ferry links the island to the south coast; expect queues.
The SGR train to Nairobi leaves from Mombasa Terminus at Miritini.
Uber and Bolt operate in the city.
food: Swahili dishes: biryani, pilau and coconut fish curry.
Street snacks like viazi karai (spiced fried potatoes) and mahamri.
Fresh seafood along the coast.
Madafu (fresh coconut water) from street sellers.
safety: Keep valuables out of sight on beaches and in crowded markets.
Use registered beach operators rather than unofficial 'beach boys' offering tours.
Dress modestly in the Old Town out of respect for local customs.

cost.reason: Cheaper than Nairobi locally; beach resorts can be pricey.

transport.reason: Tuk-tuks are easy, but ferries and traffic slow things down.

climate.reason: Hot and humid most of the year.

safety.reason: Generally relaxed; normal caution in busy areas and at night.

nightlife.reason: Beach bars and clubs, especially along the north coast.

verify: Scores are editorial estimates. Population figure is for Mombasa County.

name: Kisumu
tagline: Sunsets over Lake Victoria
intro: Kenya's third city sits on the shores of Lake Victoria, Africa's largest lake. It is relaxed, warm and known for fresh fish, lakeside restaurants and a growing waterfront.
population: ~0.6 million urban; ~1.2 million in Kisumu County (2019 census)
climate: Warm to hot all year, with rain possible in most months and heavier rains around March–May.
airport: Kisumu International Airport (KIS)

neighbourhoods.name: CBD
neighbourhoods.note: Compact, walkable centre around Oginga Odinga Street.

neighbourhoods.name: Milimani
neighbourhoods.note: Leafy, quiet residential area with guesthouses and hotels.

neighbourhoods.name: Dunga Beach
neighbourhoods.note: Fishing village on the lake, good for boat trips and fresh tilapia.

neighbourhoods.name: Hippo Point
neighbourhoods.note: Lakeside viewpoint popular for sunsets.

moneyTips: M-Pesa is used everywhere.
Prices are generally lower than in Nairobi.
Agree boat trip prices before setting out.
transport: Tuk-tuks and boda bodas are the main way to get around.
Matatus link Kisumu with other western Kenyan towns.
Uber and Bolt operate but with fewer cars than Nairobi.
Daily flights to Nairobi take about an hour.
food: Fried or stewed tilapia (fish) with ugali.
Omena (small dried fish), a local favourite.
Lakeside restaurants at Dunga and along the waterfront.
safety: Generally relaxed for visitors.
Only take lake trips with operators who provide life jackets.
Use mosquito repellent; it is a lowland lakeside area.

cost.reason: Noticeably cheaper than Nairobi.

transport.reason: Small and easy with tuk-tuks, but limited public transport.

climate.reason: Warm to hot, more humid than the highlands.

safety.reason: Generally relaxed perception among visitors.

nightlife.reason: A few lively spots and lakeside bars.

verify: Scores are editorial estimates. Check urban population figure.

name: Nakuru
tagline: Rift Valley city next to a national park
intro: A fast-growing Rift Valley town that became Kenya's fourth city in 2021. Lake Nakuru National Park, known for rhinos and flamingos, sits right on its edge.
climate: Mild and fairly dry, warm days and cool nights; rains roughly March–May and October–November.
airport: No major airport; nearest is Jomo Kenyatta International (NBO), ~160 km away

neighbourhoods.name: CBD
neighbourhoods.note: Busy town centre with markets, banks and bus stages.

neighbourhoods.name: Milimani
neighbourhoods.note: Quiet, leafy area with hotels and guesthouses.

neighbourhoods.name: Section 58
neighbourhoods.note: Residential area with a mix of hotels and restaurants.

neighbourhoods.name: Lanet
neighbourhoods.note: Growing area on the Nairobi side of town.

moneyTips: M-Pesa is used everywhere.
National park fees are set by Kenya Wildlife Service and paid electronically.
Local prices are lower than in Nairobi.
transport: Shuttles and matatus to Nairobi take about 2.5–3 hours.
Tuk-tuks and boda bodas for short trips around town.
You need a vehicle (yours or a tour's) to drive through Lake Nakuru National Park.
food: Nyama choma, a Rift Valley favourite.
Ugali, sukuma wiki and fresh milk.
Roadside roasted maize.
safety: Generally relaxed for visitors.
The highway to Nairobi is busy; travel by day where possible.
Normal caution in the busy town centre.

cost.reason: Cheaper than Nairobi for food and stays.

transport.reason: Easy within town; you need a car for the park.

climate.reason: Mild, fairly dry highland climate.

safety.reason: Generally relaxed perception.

nightlife.reason: A modest club and bar scene.

scores.vibe: Rift Valley town with big ambitions

verify: Scores are editorial estimates. Confirm city status date (2021) and travel time to Nairobi.

name: Eldoret
tagline: Home of champions
intro: A highland city in the North Rift, famous for producing world-class distance runners; nearby Iten is a training base for athletes from around the world. Eldoret was granted city status in 2024.
climate: Cool highland climate with chilly mornings; rain is common from about April to October.
airport: Eldoret International Airport (EDL)

neighbourhoods.name: CBD
neighbourhoods.note: Compact town centre with shops, banks and stages.

neighbourhoods.name: Elgon View
neighbourhoods.note: Leafy, upmarket residential area.

neighbourhoods.name: Kapsoya
neighbourhoods.note: Residential estate with local shops.

neighbourhoods.name: Iten (nearby)
neighbourhoods.note: Small town about 35 km away, the famous high-altitude running base in Elgeyo-Marakwet County.

moneyTips: M-Pesa is the normal way to pay.
Prices are lower than in Nairobi.
Carry some cash for trips to rural areas.
transport: Matatus and shuttles connect to Nairobi, Nakuru and Kisumu.
Boda bodas and tuk-tuks for local trips.
Domestic flights to Nairobi take under an hour.
food: Mursik (fermented milk), a Kalenjin speciality.
Ugali with meat or greens.
Fresh dairy from the surrounding farms.
safety: Generally relaxed for visitors.
Dress warmly in the evenings; it gets cold.
Normal caution in the busy centre.

cost.reason: Cheaper than Nairobi.

transport.reason: Small and manageable with bodas and tuk-tuks.

climate.reason: Cool and fresh, sometimes cold.

safety.reason: Generally relaxed perception.

nightlife.reason: A few local spots; quieter than bigger cities.

verify: Scores are editorial estimates. Confirm city status was granted in 2024, the Iten distance and the rainy season.

name: Kampala
tagline: Uganda's capital of hills and boda bodas
intro: Uganda's busy, friendly capital, originally built on seven hills near the shores of Lake Victoria. Known for its energy, live music and very large numbers of boda bodas.
population: ~1.8 million in the city; much more in Greater Kampala (2024 census)
climate: Warm all year, with two rainy seasons roughly March–May and September–November.
airport: Entebbe International Airport (EBB), ~40 km away

neighbourhoods.name: Kololo
neighbourhoods.note: Upmarket hill with embassies, restaurants and hotels.

neighbourhoods.name: Nakasero
neighbourhoods.note: Central hill with offices, hotels and the famous market below.

neighbourhoods.name: Kabalagala
neighbourhoods.note: Lively area known for bars and nightlife.

neighbourhoods.name: Muyenga
neighbourhoods.note: Hilly residential area with views over the lake.

neighbourhoods.name: Ntinda
neighbourhoods.note: Busy, popular residential and shopping area.

neighbourhoods.name: Bugolobi
neighbourhoods.note: Quiet residential area with cafés.

neighbourhoods.name: Old Kampala
neighbourhoods.note: Historic area with the Gaddafi National Mosque, offering city views.

MTN MoMo and Airtel Money are widely used.
Check notes carefully; denominations look similar at first.
Older or damaged US dollar notes are often refused at forex bureaus.
transport: Boda bodas are everywhere; app-based ones (SafeBoda, Uber, Bolt) let you agree prices and get a helmet.
Shared minibuses are called 'taxis' in Uganda; private cars are 'special hire'.
Traffic jams are heavy at peak times.
Allow at least an hour to reach Entebbe airport, more at rush hour.
food: Rolex: an omelette rolled in a chapati, the city's favourite snack.
Matoke (steamed green bananas) with groundnut sauce.
Luwombo, a stew steamed in banana leaves.
Fresh tilapia from Lake Victoria.
safety: Normal big-city caution with phones and bags in crowds.
Ask boda drivers for a helmet, or choose app-based riders.
Use registered taxis or apps at night.

cost.reason: Generally cheaper than Nairobi for food and transport.

transport.reason: Plenty of bodas, but heavy traffic and few formal options.

climate.reason: Warm and pleasant, with frequent rain showers.

safety.reason: Normal big-city caution; traffic is the bigger day-to-day risk.

nightlife.reason: Known across the region for its late, lively nightlife.

scores.vibe: Friendly, loud and full of life

verify: Scores are editorial estimates. Confirm 2024 census population for Kampala city.

name: Entebbe
tagline: Uganda's airport town on Lake Victoria
intro: A calm, green town on a peninsula in Lake Victoria, home to Uganda's main international airport and State House. Many visitors spend their first or last night here.
climate: Warm and humid, cooled by the lake; two rainy seasons roughly March–May and September–November.
airport: Entebbe International Airport (EBB)

neighbourhoods.name: Town centre
neighbourhoods.note: Small centre with shops, banks and restaurants.

neighbourhoods.name: Botanical Gardens area
neighbourhoods.note: Leafy lakeside area with old trees, birds and monkeys.

neighbourhoods.name: Kitooro
neighbourhoods.note: Local market and shopping area.

neighbourhoods.name: Lido / lakeside beaches
neighbourhoods.note: Lake beaches popular at weekends.

moneyTips: Change only what you need at the airport; rates in town are often better.
MTN MoMo and Airtel Money are widely used.
Keep some small notes for boda rides.
transport: Boda bodas and special hire taxis for short trips.
The Kampala–Entebbe Expressway makes the trip to the capital quicker.
Boats run to Ngamba Island chimpanzee sanctuary.
food: Fresh tilapia and Nile perch by the lake.
Rolex from street stalls.
Lakeside restaurants and hotel terraces.
safety: Generally calm and relaxed.
Swimming in the lake is not recommended because of bilharzia risk.

transport.reason: Small town, easy by boda or taxi.

climate.reason: Warm, with lake breezes.

safety.reason: Calm, relaxed town feel.

nightlife.reason: Quiet; a few lakeside bars.

name: Jinja
tagline: Where the Nile begins its journey
intro: A riverside city near the point where the Nile leaves Lake Victoria. Known for adventure activities on the river and a relaxed, old-fashioned town centre. Jinja was given city status in 2020.
climate: Warm all year with two rainy seasons, similar to Kampala.
airport: No major airport; nearest is Entebbe International (EBB), ~120 km by road

neighbourhoods.name: Town centre
neighbourhoods.note: Old colonial and Indian-style shopfronts along Main Street.

neighbourhoods.name: Source of the Nile
neighbourhoods.note: Riverside area with boat trips to the source.

neighbourhoods.name: Bujagali
neighbourhoods.note: Riverside area with lodges and adventure operators.

neighbourhoods.name: Nalufenya
neighbourhoods.note: Residential area close to the river.

moneyTips: Adventure activities are usually priced in US dollars.
MTN MoMo and Airtel Money work for most local spending.
Local food and transport are cheap.
transport: Boda bodas for short trips.
Shared taxis and buses to Kampala take about 2–3 hours, depending on traffic.
Many lodges arrange transfers.
food: Rolex, said to have become popular in the Jinja area.
Fresh fish from the lake and river.
Backpacker cafés and riverside restaurants.
safety: Generally relaxed.
Use reputable adventure operators with good safety records.

transport.reason: Small town, but mostly bodas and lodge transfers.

climate.reason: Warm and pleasant.

safety.reason: Relaxed small-city feel.

nightlife.reason: A few backpacker bars.

name: Dar es Salaam
tagline: Tanzania's busy harbour city
intro: Tanzania's largest city and commercial capital, on the Indian Ocean. (The official capital is Dodoma.) It is hot, busy and the main gateway to Zanzibar by ferry.
population: ~5.4 million (2022 census, Dar es Salaam Region)
climate: Hot and humid all year. Long rains roughly March–May, short rains roughly November–December. Coolest around June–August.
airport: Julius Nyerere International Airport (DAR)

neighbourhoods.name: City Centre (Posta)
neighbourhoods.note: Offices, ferry terminal and the old waterfront.

neighbourhoods.name: Kariakoo
neighbourhoods.note: Huge, busy market district; great for shopping, very crowded.

neighbourhoods.name: Masaki
neighbourhoods.note: Upmarket peninsula with restaurants, hotels and embassies.

neighbourhoods.name: Oyster Bay
neighbourhoods.note: Leafy, upmarket area with a beach promenade (Coco Beach).

neighbourhoods.name: Mikocheni
neighbourhoods.note: Residential area with shops and offices.

neighbourhoods.name: Mbezi Beach

neighbourhoods.name: Kigamboni
neighbourhoods.note: Across the harbour, with quieter beaches; reached by ferry or bridge.

Older or damaged US dollar notes are often refused.
Carry small notes for bajajis and street food.

Bajajis (three-wheelers) and bodaboda for short trips.

Buy ferry tickets only at the official ticket offices, not from touts.

transport.reason: BRT and apps help, but traffic is heavy.

climate.reason: Hot and humid most of the year.

safety.reason: Normal big-city caution needed.

nightlife.reason: Plenty of bars and live music, especially at weekends.

verify: Scores are editorial estimates. Population is for Dar es Salaam Region (2022 census); confirm.

name: Arusha
tagline: Safari capital at the foot of Mount Meru
intro: A highland city in northern Tanzania and the starting point for safaris to the Serengeti, Ngorongoro and Tarangire. Mount Meru rises behind it, and Kilimanjaro is not far away.
climate: Mild, with warm days and cool nights; long rains roughly March–May and short rains around November.
airport: Kilimanjaro International Airport (JRO), ~50 km away; Arusha Airport (ARK) for domestic and safari flights

name: Zanzibar City
tagline: Stone Town's winding lanes and spice-scented air

climate: Hot and humid; long rains roughly March–May, short rains around November. Cooler and breezier around June–October.
airport: Abeid Amani Karume International Airport (ZNZ)

neighbourhoods.note: The UNESCO-listed old town: narrow lanes, history and boutique hotels.

neighbourhoods.note: The main market, busy with spices, fruit and fish.

neighbourhoods.name: Michenzani / Ng'ambo

airport: Kigali International Airport (KGL)

neighbourhoods.name: Nyamirambo

name: Addis Ababa
tagline: High-altitude capital with its own calendar and clock
intro: Ethiopia's capital and the seat of the African Union, high in the highlands. Ethiopia uses its own calendar (several years behind the Gregorian one) and a 12-hour clock that starts at sunrise, so check whether times are in 'Ethiopian' or 'international' time.
population: ~5 million+ (estimate; the last full census was in 2007)
climate: Cool and mild thanks to the altitude; the main rainy season is roughly June–September.
airport: Addis Ababa Bole International Airport (ADD)

neighbourhoods.name: Bole
neighbourhoods.note: Near the airport: hotels, cafés, restaurants and nightlife.

neighbourhoods.name: Piassa
neighbourhoods.note: Old commercial centre with historic buildings and cafés.

neighbourhoods.name: Kazanchis
neighbourhoods.note: Business area with hotels and offices.

neighbourhoods.name: Merkato

neighbourhoods.name: Sarbet
